conversation.user: I am an international applicant interested in the Smart Grid Systems and Technologies Master of Engineering. Is it available to international applicants?
conversation.advisor:
Yes. The **full-time blended** Smart Grid Systems and Technologies Master of Engineering is available to international applicants. The **part-time online** option is not available internationally. A valid BCIT study permit is required before starting the full-time program.

[View the program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/smart-grid-systems-and-technologies-master-of-engineering-full-time-part-time-m500meng/)

For more information, see BCIT International Students: https://www.bcit.ca/international-students/.

expectation.question: I am an international applicant interested in the Smart Grid Systems and Technologies Master of Engineering. Is it available to international applicants?
expectation.expected: Use this program's INTERNATIONAL evidence. Distinguish available, restricted, not accepted, and unknown; never infer ineligibility from silence.

conversation.user: So does that automatically mean I'm admitted?
conversation.advisor:
No. Being eligible to apply as an international applicant does **not** mean automatic admission. Admission is competitive: you must meet the entrance requirements, submit a complete application, and be selected by the Graduate Selection Committee. You are admitted only if BCIT issues an offer of acceptance.

[Review the program’s admission requirements](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/smart-grid-systems-and-technologies-master-of-engineering-full-time-part-time-m500meng/)

expectation.question: So does that automatically mean I'm admitted?
expectation.expected: No. Separate international availability from individual admission, competition, and human verification. Do not guarantee admission.

conversation.user: What can you actually verify, and what should I confirm with BCIT?
conversation.advisor:
**I can verify:**

- This is an active **Master of Engineering** program delivered through BCIT’s School of Energy at Burnaby, with blended full-time and part-time formats.
- Standard entry requires a bachelor’s degree in electrical or electronics engineering with at least a **2.4/4.0 GPA (60%)**, plus the stated graduate English requirement.
- Alternate entry may be available for specified related degrees, subject to a pre-entry assessment and possible bridging courses.
- Admission is competitive and decided by the Graduate Selection Committee.
- The curriculum includes required courses such as **SGST 9110 – Introduction to Smart Electricity Grids**, **SGST 9210 – Advanced Power Systems Analysis**, and **SGST 9340 – Energy Storage & Power Electronics**. Term 4 listings include **SGST 9410 – Capstone Project** and **SGST 9430 – Directed Studies in Smart Grid (Elective Course)**.

**You should confirm with BCIT:**

- Whether your particular degree, calculated GPA, and English evidence meet the requirements.
- Whether you need an ICES credential evaluation, pre-entry assessment, or bridging courses.
- Whether your application and supporting documents are complete and competitive. Only BCIT can make the admission decision.
- Study-permit matters with BCIT and immigration authorities, and final PGWP eligibility with IRCC.

[BCIT program page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/smart-grid-systems-and-technologies-master-of-engineering-full-time-part-time-m500meng/)

programs.program_overview: The Master of Engineering in Smart Grid Systems and Technologies (MEng SGST) is a unique graduate program aimed at providing students with the competencies required to conduct research, plan, design, implement, maintain, commission, and operate Smart Grid systems and applications in the electric utility and related sectors. Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: blended. See details . About the program The MEng in SGST program leverages BCIT’s decade long research results, domain expertise, world-class infrastructure, seasoned faculty, and strategic partnerships with industry. Graduates of MEng in SGST will develop hands-on knowledge and understanding of foundational concepts involved in Smart Grid technologies employed in Critical Infrastructure, including applications in renewable energies, green transportation, and smart cities. Who it’s for The program caters to professionals currently employed in the industry, as well as those interested in continuing their education. As a BCIT Full-Time program, MEng SGST enables students to enrich and complement their Smart Grid domain knowledge outside normal working hours without interfering with their current jobs, thereby preparing them for exciting future careers in the carbon-constrained economy of the new millennia. MEng SGST’s learning outcomes are achieved through a combination of theoretical studies, complemented with hands-on project work at BCIT or in industry. What grads can do The program prepares students with the skills and capacity to combine knowledge from several areas traditionally taught in separate programs, including electrical power systems, computer science, and ICT (information and communications technology) to address strategic challenges, which the utility industry across the world faces in reducing its carbon footprint and transitioning to Green Economy. Next up Entrance Requirements
programs.notes: Program length This program is offered in both a flexible learning and full-time basis. Students have a maximum of five years to complete the program requirements. Program delivery Blended: This program is delivered partly on campus and partly online. Some course lectures (less than 50%) may be delivered online. Also, the MEng SGST courses are available to those who want to take individual courses for professional development. Delivery methods for each course will be tailored to specific learning outcomes. Less than 50% of the course lectures may be offered online. Courses are delivered in a format that combines online synchronous and asynchronous learning activities, team-based and individual projects, and laboratory experience with the SGST equipment and apparatus accessible remotely. Given the significance of BCIT’s current training assets on Burnaby campus, efforts are underway to make such assets safely and securely accessible to students as virtual platforms. Program location Burnaby Campus 3700 Willingdon Avenue Burnaby, BC Program structure Components Credits 1. Course work Applications (9.0) Interfaces (9.0) Components (9.0) 27.0 2. academic_rule_sets.notes: Scheduled intakes September each year. Application processing Applications are accepted: October 1st* to April 15th* April 16th* to June 30th* July 1st* to August 15th* *or next business day This program has multiple application deadlines and may fill after each deadline date. We recommend that you apply early. All supporting documents must be submitted by the application deadline. Entrance requirements Competitive Entry: Two-step process Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Graduate Studies – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Entry options: one of the following: Option 1: standard entry Post-secondary education: bachelor’s degree in electrical or electronics engineering, with a minimum GPA of 2.4 out of 4.0 (60%) based on the entire program. Option 2: alternate entry Alternate entry is for applicants who do not have a bachelor's degree in electrical or electronic engineering and may need to take bridging courses before being accepted to the program. Applicants are required to have the following: Post-secondary education: bachelor's degree with a minimum GPA of 2.4 out of 4.0 (60%) in a relevant discipline, such as: software engineering, computer engineering, computer science, physics, mathematics, information, or communications technology. Alternate entry applicants must complete a Pre-entry Assessment form to have their education, experience, and interest assessed by the program. After the review, bridging courses may be recommended for the applicant to take to apply for the program. Email a completed Pre-entry Assessment form [PDF] to: meng_sgst@bcit.ca . You may be requested to send additional documents or meet with the Program Head. Once your pre-entry assessment has been approved, submit it to your online application. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Step 2: Department Review All complete applications will be reviewed by the Graduate Selection Committee and ranked on a competitive basis. Applicants who are best suited for success in the program will be offered acceptance. Only complete applications that include all the required supporting documentation will be evaluated. For engineering disciplines outside of electrical and electronics, you may be required to—or it may be identified that you need to—take a bridging course to get accepted and succeed in the program. We have developed and recommend ELEX 0101 - Modern Power System and Circuit Fundamentals or ELEX 0102 - Fundamentals of Power Systems and Circuits that provide the fundamentals of electric circuits and systems. Recommended for success Applicants with sufficient knowledge base in electrical power systems, computer science, or ICT (information and communications technology) will have a higher chance of being successful in this program. Since admission into the program will be on a competitive basis, applicants with relevant industry experience will have an advantage due to the applied nature of the program. International applicants The full-time blended delivery option is available to international applicants. The part-time online delivery option is not available to international applicants. View available programs . Study permit: A valid BCIT study permit is required prior to starting the full-time program. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : Only the full-time option of this program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a master's degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a master’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. To submit your application: Include proof of meeting all entrance requirements. Convert all transcripts and supporting documents to PDF files . Have a credit card ready to pay the application fee. Apply Now Learn more about how to apply myCommunication Within two business days of submitting your completed application, BCIT will send a message to your personal and myBCIT email addresses. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. Go back Overview Next up Costs & Supplies

Entrance requirements Competitive Entry: Two-step process Step 1: Meet the following entrance requirements English language proficiency: Graduate Studies – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Entry options: one of the following: Option 1: standard entry Post-secondary education: bachelor’s degree in electrical or electronics engineering, with a minimum GPA of 2.4 out of 4.0 (60%) based on the entire program. Option 2: alternate entry Alternate entry is for applicants who do not have a bachelor's degree in electrical or electronic engineering and may need to take bridging courses before being accepted to the program. Applicants are required to have the following: Post-secondary education: bachelor's degree with a minimum GPA of 2.4 out of 4.0 (60%) in a relevant discipline, such as: software engineering, computer engineering, computer science, physics, mathematics, information, or communications technology. Alternate entry applicants must complete a Pre-entry Assessment form to have their education, experience, and interest assessed by the program. After the review, bridging courses may be recommended for the applicant to take to apply for the program. Email a completed Pre-entry Assessment form [PDF] to: meng_sgst@bcit.ca . You may be requested to send additional documents or meet with the Program Head. Once your pre-entry assessment has been approved, submit it to your online application. Applicants who have completed post-secondary studies outside of Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or New Zealand will require a comprehensive evaluation of their credentials by the International Credential Evaluation Service (ICES) . Credential evaluation reports from other Canadian services may be considered. Read more about how to meet BCIT’s entrance requirements Step 2: Department Review All complete applications will be reviewed by the Graduate Selection Committee and ranked on a competitive basis. Applicants who are best suited for success in the program will be offered acceptance. Only complete applications that include all the required supporting documentation will be evaluated. For engineering disciplines outside of electrical and electronics, you may be required to—or it may be identified that you need to—take a bridging course to get accepted and succeed in the program. We have developed and recommend ELEX 0101 - Modern Power System and Circuit Fundamentals or ELEX 0102 - Fundamentals of Power Systems and Circuits that provide the fundamentals of electric circuits and systems. Recommended for success Applicants with sufficient knowledge base in electrical power systems, computer science, or ICT (information and communications technology) will have a higher chance of being successful in this program. Since admission into the program will be on a competitive basis, applicants with relevant industry experience will have an advantage due to the applied nature of the program. International applicants The full-time blended delivery option is available to international applicants. The part-time online delivery option is not available to international applicants. Post-graduation Work Permit (PGWP) eligibility : Only the full-time option of this program currently meets the PGWP eligibility requirements based on study program - graduates with a master's degree and is eligible for students to apply for a PGWP. There are no field of study requirements (CIP) for graduates with a master’s degree. Students are responsible for meeting all Immigration, Refugees, and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) PGWP eligibility requirements . Final PGWP approval is at the discretion of IRCC. Apply to program Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. All correspondence regarding your application will be posted to your online myCommunication account at my.bcit.ca . We will send you an email when a new message is posted. It is important to watch for these emails or regularly check your account online. You can expect to receive communication concerning the status of your application within four weeks. program.program_overview: The Master of Engineering in Smart Grid Systems and Technologies (MEng SGST) is a unique graduate program aimed at providing students with the competencies required to conduct research, plan, design, implement, maintain, commission, and operate Smart Grid systems and applications in the electric utility and related sectors. Note: The September 2026 intake is now closed for new applications. Applications for the September 2027 intake will be accepted starting October 1, 2026. Delivery: blended. See details . About the program The MEng in SGST program leverages BCIT’s decade long research results, domain expertise, world-class infrastructure, seasoned faculty, and strategic partnerships with industry. Graduates of MEng in SGST will develop hands-on knowledge and understanding of foundational concepts involved in Smart Grid technologies employed in Critical Infrastructure, including applications in renewable energies, green transportation, and smart cities. Who it’s for The program caters to professionals currently employed in the industry, as well as those interested in continuing their education. As a BCIT Full-Time program, MEng SGST enables students to enrich and complement their Smart Grid domain knowledge outside normal working hours without interfering with their current jobs, thereby preparing them for exciting future careers in the carbon-constrained economy of the new millennia. MEng SGST’s learning outcomes are achieved through a combination of theoretical studies, complemented with hands-on project work at BCIT or in industry. What grads can do The program prepares students with the skills and capacity to combine knowledge from several areas traditionally taught in separate programs, including electrical power systems, computer science, and ICT (information and communications technology) to address strategic challenges, which the utility industry across the world faces in reducing its carbon footprint and transitioning to Green Economy.
